verdict.reasoning: Patient reports knee pain with clicking and duration about two weeks: “my knees are hurting and they're clicking a lot… I can't run very far anymore without just feeling pain in my knees” and later clarifies “It's actually my right knee that hurts,” and onset “probably it's been about two weeks.”

She reports tingling in right toes and that it is not ongoing: “sometimes I also get this weird tingling in my toes” and later specifies “after the run, there was tingling in my toes, like, on my, you know, my right toes… it was just that time.” This supports intermittent right toe tingling.

She is training for a marathon with increased running and describes distances: “I'm currently training for a marathon… I'm trying to run like… maybe like seven or eight miles… I started about maybe a month ago. I've done like… four or five miles and I've just done like a couple of seven mile runs.”
Onset timing is given: “I would say it probably starts like after maybe 20 minutes or so, which is probably… around mile three, maybe and a half or three miles.”
She says the pain has led her to stop: In response to whether she has to stop, she says “the last time I actually stopped… then I stopped because it was… I feel like it's getting worse.”

She links clicking with flexion/extension during abs: “when I do my abs, it kind of requires me to… go from the flex position of my knees and straighten my legs. Then I hear all this clicking.” She also notes it with flex and extend in general context.

Initial mild swelling improved with ice: “Does the knee look swollen?” / “Well, it did. Like, the first time I ran, it was a little bit swollen, but then I just put some, like, ice on it and it went away.” The knee discussed is the symptomatic right knee.
No current pain at rest: “right now, right now it's not swollen. And right now it doesn't hurt, you know, but it just kind of comes on when… when I run, it will start hurting.”
Prior fall with bruise during ice hockey: “I play some ice hockey and I had this injury a few months ago… I just like fell on the ice and… had a huge bruise.”

She describes intermittent swelling of legs/feet via sock marks: “if you stand for a long time, your feet will kind of… or your legs will swell up? Like, I notice it because of my socks. I'll just kind of notice this indentation.”
Single episode of right toe tingling after a run: “there was this tingling in my toes. Like, after the run, there was tingling in my toes, like, on my… my right toes… it was just that time.”
Denies calf pain: When asked “any pain in the back of the calf or anything like that?” she replies “No, nothing like that? No.”

The assessment statement summarizes what is reported: right knee pain, mechanical clicking, onset around two weeks (“probably it's been about two weeks”) after increased running (“started about maybe a month ago… seven or eight miles”), intermittent swelling (“it was a little bit swollen… it went away”) and activity-related pain limiting running (“I can't run very far anymore… the last time I actually stopped”). The suspicion of overuse from increased training is a direct clinical inference from her marathon training and symptom onset after runs; the prior knee contusion is documented (“fell on the ice and… had a huge bruise”) and may contribute. The transcript does not contradict this interpretation.

Advice to continue ice and modify running: “definitely carrying on with the ice therapy that you've been using… as much as you can use the ice… I would try and ease up on the running if you can. And if it's painful enough that you're having to stop running, then it's not a good idea to do that.”
